published_statement: Abstract: 'We construct a model for the nucleation of a wormhole within a Lorentzian spacetime by employing techniques from topological surgery and Morse theory. In our framework, a 0-surgery process describes the neighborhood of the nucleation point inside a compact region of spacetime, yielding a singular Lorentzian cobordism that connects two spacelike regions with different topologies. To avoid the singularity at the critical point of the Morse function, we employ the Misner trick of taking a connected sum with a closed 4-manifold -- namely CP^2 -- to obtain an everywhere nondegenerate Lorentzian metric. This connected sum replaces the naked singularity with a region containing closed timelike curves. The obtained spacetime is nonsingular, but violates all the standard energy conditions.' Sec. IV.B: the Morse spacetime (13) has type-IV regions by criterion (19) (Fig. 9) and 'violates all the standard energy conditions'. Sec. IV.C: 'we find regions where T_mu nu w^mu w^nu < 0' (Fig. 12); a type-IV point p=(1,0,0,0) on CP^2; eq. (24): 'the numerical factor 2 is arbitrary and can be replaced by any real number zeta > 1 ... changing zeta merely shifts, thins, or expands the regions where the energy conditions are violated; it does not eliminate them altogether.' Sec. V.D: homotopies H1-H4 with smooth monotone b(eta), c(eta) and a path alpha(eta) in SO(4), 'Because the entire deformation is smooth and nonsingular, the resulting Lorentzian metric on the neck remains free of singularities, and no further explicit expression is required for our purposes.' Sec. I: 'The conclusions we present, apart from the investigations of the energy conditions on these spacetimes, are purely kinematic'.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the authors had: no empirical input at all -- the result is kinematic/topological (integers: chi, kink, degree, u-invariant) plus a pointwise Hawking-Ellis classification of the Einstein tensor of a constructed metric. What came later: nothing observational bears on it; the only 'later' items are 2026 topic-adjacent papers not read here. Does missing data change the conclusion? Evidence AGAINST: every topological claim is an integer re-derived exactly (C1, C2, C8); the EC classification is re-derived in closed form, D = 4P/(F^2(F+1)^4) (C5c), and holds for every Lambda > 0 (Lambda only scales CP^2; C9). The one moved-looking item is a scale-convention slip in (23)/(28) (C10a'), a discrepancy, not a refutation. Evidence FOR incompleteness (not wrongness): what the authors lacked is COMPUTATION, not data -- no integrated energy figure, no magnitude of T in the type-IV band (C5e/C5g show the band runs along the whole critical level set, so any integral depends on W's extent), several C^1 matchings asserted rather than shown, and the QFT back-reaction on the compactly generated Cauchy horizon explicitly excluded (P10). So the paper is incomplete in exactly the ways formation.py already records (OPEN, not priced), plus the scope exclusions the tree does not carry.
